speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. I see you have generalized fatigue and severe itching alongside abnormal liver function tests. To begin narrowing down the cause, have you noticed any dark urine, pale stools, or changes in your stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of ulcerative colitis combined with abnormal liver tests raises a strong suspicion of primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC). Given your sexual history, we must also rule out viral hepatitis and HIV. REQUEST TEST: Liver panel including Alk Phos, Bilirubin, AST, ALT, and Viral Hepatitis A, B, C, E serologies. REQUEST TEST: HIV antibody/antigen test.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver Panel - Alkaline Phosphatase: 460 U/L, Total Bilirubin: 1.5 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin: 0.9 mg/dL, AST: 75 U/L, ALT: 78 U/L. Viral Hepatitis A, B, C, E serologies: Not explicitly listed in the provided data. HIV antibody/antigen test: Not explicitly listed in the provided data.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, Ulcerative Colitis Social history: Sexually active with inconsistent condom use

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, diarrhea, joint pain, or recent travel. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC)

REQUEST IMAGES: MRCP (Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography) of the biliary tree.

While your previous doctor suspected pneumonia, your severe itching and abnormal liver tests point strongly toward a biliary or autoimmune liver disease; please note that a diagnosis of pneumonia would not explain these specific findings.
